title: The Go Programming Language Specification
why: The normative definition of Go's tokens, its longest-match rule, automatic semicolon insertion and the reserved keyword list.

title: ISO/IEC 9899:201x (C11) Committee Draft N1570
why: Text of C 6.4: the longest-match rule for forming preprocessing tokens and the x+++++y tokenization example.

claim: Go breaks the input into tokens by taking the longest sequence of characters that forms a valid token as the next token.
quote: While breaking the input into tokens, the next token is the longest sequence of characters that form a valid token.

claim: Go automatically inserts a semicolon into the token stream immediately after a line's final token when that token is an identifier, an integer, floating-point, imaginary, rune, or string literal, one of the keywords break, continue, fallthrough or return, or one of the operators and punctuation ++, --, ), ] or }.
quote:
When the input is broken into tokens, a semicolon is automatically inserted into the token stream immediately after a line's final token if that token is
- an identifier
- an integer, floating-point, imaginary, rune, or string literal
- one of the keywords break, continue, fallthrough, or return
- one of the operators and punctuation ++, --, ), ], or }

claim: Go reserves 25 keywords, none of which may be used as identifiers.
quote:
The following keywords are reserved and may not be used as identifiers.

break        default      func         interface    select
case         defer        go           map          struct
chan         else         goto         package      switch
const        fallthrough  if           range        type
continue     for          import       return       var

claim: Once the input stream has been parsed into preprocessing tokens up to a given character, the next preprocessing token is the longest sequence of characters that could constitute a preprocessing token.
quote: If the input stream has been parsed into preprocessing tokens up to a given character, the next preprocessing token is the longest sequence of characters that could constitute a preprocessing token.

claim: C parses the fragment x+++++y as x ++ ++ + y, which violates a constraint on increment operators, even though the parse x ++ + ++ y might yield a correct expression.
quote: The program fragment x+++++y is parsed as x ++ ++ + y, which violates a constraint on increment operators, even though the parse x ++ + ++ y might yield a correct expression.

claim: The scanner reads a stream of characters and produces a stream of words, aggregating characters into words, applying rules to decide whether each word is legal in the source language, and assigning a valid word a syntactic category.
quote: The scanner, or lexical analyzer, reads a stream of characters and produces a stream of words. It aggregates characters to form words and applies a set of rules to determine whether or not each word is legal in the source language. If the word is valid, the scanner assigns it a syntactic category, or part of speech.

claim: Although efficient parsing techniques weakened the original efficiency argument for separating scanning from parsing, scanners are still built separately because it provides a clean separation of concerns between lexical structure and syntactic structure.
quote: The advent of efficient parsing techniques weakened this argument, but the practice of building scanners persists because it provides a clean separation of concerns between lexical structure and syntactic structure.
